analysis.evidence: The relative clause אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבֹדוּ identifies the nation that Abram’s descendants will serve. אֶת marks that nation as the object of God’s judgment.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine singular absolute noun.
analysis.sense: a people counted as a nation

analysis.evidence: In הַגּוֹי אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבֹדוּ, “the nation that they will serve,” אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause in which הַגּוֹי supplies the understood object of יַעֲבֹדוּ.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Abram’s descendants are the subject of יַעֲבֹדוּ. The relative clause אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבֹדוּ identifies הַגּוֹי as the nation they will serve. God says he will judge that nation, after which the descendants will leave.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine plural, with future reference.

analysis.evidence: וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן means “and after that.” It places the departure expressed by יֵצְאוּ after the judgment announced in דָּן אָנֹכִי.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ (“and”) prefixes אַחֲרֵי, the preposition governing כֵן (“that”).
